newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal 97 budget gap may be below target-Finmin.
newsitem.headline: Portugal 97 budget gap may be below target-Finmin.

text.p: Portugal's budget deficit in 1997 may be less than the government's target of 2.9 percent of gross domestic product (GDP), Finance Minister Antonio Sousa Franco said.
"It is very early to make forecasts (but) I think that it is possible (to have a deficit below target) just as happened last year," he told journalists.
The minister also said that the indications were that economic growth in 1996 was higher than the government's forecast 2.75 percent.
"Everything points to the Portuguese economy last year having grown more than the government's target," Sousa Franco said.
He said that he had received a report from an independent research body indicating the economy could have grown by three percent in 1996.
"We do not know if this estimate is fully confirmed but in 1997 and subsequent years, the conditions are there for a high level of growth," Sousa Franco said.
The higher the rate of growth, the better chance Portugal had of achieving its budget deficit target with something to spare, the minister added.
